extra.message: User input from the 'id' query parameter (params['id'][0]) is concatenated directly into a SQL query string passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via /users?id=1 UNION SELECT ... to read or modify the database (CWE-89).

The 'msg' query parameter is returned from XSSReflected.run() without any HTML escaping and is later interpolated into the page template via str.format(). This allows reflected XSS, e.g. /post?msg=<script>alert(1)</script> (CWE-79).

Comments stored in the database (inserted via /guestbook?comment=...) are rendered into HTML with '{}'.format(column) without escaping. This allows stored XSS that executes for any visitor viewing the guestbook (CWE-79).

The 'path' query parameter is interpolated unescaped into a JavaScript window.location.replace('{path}') call via str.format(). This enables both unvalidated open redirect (CWE-601) and XSS by breaking out of the JS string, e.g. /jump?path=');alert(1)// (CWE-79).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The /admin route (ExecutionAfterRedirect.run) renders administrative content to every requester and only guards it with a client-side window.location redirect when no cookie is present. There is no server-side authorization check, so unauthenticated users receive the protected admin content (Execution After Redirect / CWE-862).

The 'domain' query parameter is concatenated with a command name and passed to subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters, e.g. /diag?domain=example.com;whoami, achieving remote command execution (CWE-78).

The 'object' query parameter is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads(). Because pickle can invoke arbitrary code via __reduce__, an attacker can craft a payload that executes arbitrary code on the server (RCE), as demonstrated by the RCE.__reduce__ class in the same module (CWE-502).

The 'path' query parameter is passed to open(os.path.abspath(path), 'rb') without validating that it stays within an allowed directory. os.path.abspath does not prevent traversal, so /docs?path=../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary files (CWE-22).

When the 'path' parameter contains '://', it is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(path). This lets an attacker make the server fetch arbitrary URLs (internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, etc.), resulting in Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918).

The session cookie SESSIONID is set to a value supplied via the 'session' query parameter (cookie['SESSIONID'] = session). This allows session fixation: an attacker forces a known session ID on a victim, who then logs in, after which the attacker reuses that ID (CWE-384).

In SessionFixation.run the 'path' query parameter is interpolated into window.location = '{path}' via str.format() without escaping. This allows unvalidated open redirect (CWE-601) and XSS by breaking out of the JS string (CWE-79).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: SessionHijacking.run renders the logged-in user's firstname, lastname and email into HTML with str.format() without escaping. The email field is user-controllable (via /settings), enabling stored XSS when the user (or a CSRF-forced victim) views /profile (CWE-79).

In AuthBypass.run the username (only stripped of non-word chars) and the raw password are concatenated directly into a SQL query. An attacker can bypass authentication with a payload such as password=' OR '1'='1, yielding SQL injection and authentication bypass (CWE-89).
A hardcoded backdoor credential is checked in code: if username == 'dsvpwa' and password == 'dsvpwa'. Anyone knowing these values can authenticate without a database lookup (CWE-798).

On a sqlite3.OperationalError the exception object 'e' (whose message contains the malformed SQL including attacker-supplied input) is reflected into the page via content.format(type=type, message=e) without escaping, enabling reflected XSS and information disclosure through error messages (CWE-79, CWE-209).

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: XSRequestForgery.run performs a state-changing operation (UPDATE users SET email) based solely on a GET query parameter with no CSRF token or origin verification. An attacker can force a logged-in victim's browser to update their email via a crafted link/image, e.g. /settings?email=attacker@evil (CWE-352).

XSRequestForgery.render renders the user's firstname, lastname and email into input value="{}" attributes via str.format() without escaping. Since email is user-controllable, an attacker can inject value="><script>...</script> to achieve stored XSS on the /settings page (CWE-79).

Clickjacking.run deletes the logged-in user's account based on a GET query parameter (delete=1) with no CSRF protection. An attacker can cause account deletion by embedding /danger?delete=1 in a page visited by a logged-in victim (CWE-352).

StaticHandler.find opens files using open('./{}'.format(path)) where path is the raw request path with no sanitization or traversal restriction (the same pattern repeats on line 118). Requesting /../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary files outside the static directory (CWE-22).

do_BDR passes the raw request path (self.path[1:]) to subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True). Sending a BDR HTTP request with a crafted path executes arbitrary shell commands on the server, e.g. BDR /whoami or BDR /;cat /etc/passwd, with no authentication required (CWE-78).

Session identifiers are generated with random.sample (Mersenne Twister PRNG) instead of a cryptographically secure generator (secrets). The resulting SESSIONID tokens are predictable, undermining session security (CWE-330).

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The SESSIONID session cookie is emitted via send_header('Set-Cookie', morsel.OutputString()) having only 'path' set; neither the Secure nor the HttpOnly attribute is configured. This exposes the session token to interception over HTTP and to theft via document.cookie in XSS attacks (CWE-614, CWE-1004).

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The response sets X-XSS-Protection: 0, explicitly disabling the browser's reflected-XSS auditor and weakening defense-in-depth alongside the application's XSS sinks (CWE-16).

The Content-Security-Policy is set to "default-src * 'unsafe-inline'", allowing scripts from any origin and inline script execution. This effectively disables CSP as an XSS mitigation and is also missing a frame-ancestors directive, facilitating clickjacking (CWE-16, CWE-1021).

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
